practice_impact: Know that IRA negotiation is in effect and the Part D out-of-pocket cap exists. These are relevant to healthcare systems and access questions.
source: CMS, Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program: Negotiated Prices for Initial Price Applicability Year 2026 (fact sheet), 2024

change: On November 8, 2024 the FDA issued a proposed order to remove oral phenylephrine from the OTC nasal decongestant monograph because it is not effective at oral doses. No final order was confirmed as of October 2026, so products may still be marketed.
practice_impact: Oral phenylephrine is ineffective as a decongestant. Recommend pseudoephedrine (behind-the-counter, CMEA limits) or intranasal decongestants or steroids instead. Intranasal phenylephrine is unaffected.
source: FDA press announcement, FDA Proposes Ending Use of Oral Phenylephrine as OTC Monograph Nasal Decongestant Active Ingredient, 2024

change: On January 13, 2026 the FDA requested removal of the suicidal behavior and ideation warning from the weight-management GLP-1 RA labels (Saxenda, Wegovy, Zepbound). A meta-analysis of 91 trials with about 108,000 participants and claims data showed no increased risk. This aligns the weight-management labels with the diabetes GLP-1 labels.
practice_impact: Suicidality monitoring is no longer a labeled warning for GLP-1 obesity products. General depression screening remains good practice.
source: FDA, FDA Requests Removal of Suicidal Behavior and Ideation Warning from GLP-1 RA Medications, 2026

change: On February 28, 2025 the FDA announced class-wide testosterone labeling changes based on TRAVERSE, which found no increase in MACE. It recommended adding TRAVERSE results and removing the boxed warning language on adverse CV outcomes, while keeping the Limitation of Use for age-related hypogonadism. It required BP-increase warnings for all products, including product-specific ABPM data.
practice_impact: Testosterone replacement in true hypogonadism is not linked to increased MACE (TRAVERSE). Monitor BP, hematocrit, and PSA. The secondary-exposure boxed warning for gels remains.
source: FDA, FDA Issues Class-Wide Labeling Changes for Testosterone Products, 2025

change: On June 27, 2025 the FDA eliminated the REMS for all approved autologous CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T therapies: Abecma, Breyanzi, Carvykti, Kymriah, Tecartus, and Yescarta. Site certification and the tocilizumab on-hand requirement were removed. The post-infusion proximity period was shortened from 4 to 2 weeks, and the driving restriction from 8 to 2 weeks.
practice_impact: CAR-T products no longer require REMS certification. CRS and ICANS management with tocilizumab and steroids remains essential. Patients now stay near the center for 2 weeks and avoid driving for 2 weeks.
source: FDA action eliminating REMS for autologous CAR T-cell immunotherapies, 2025 (AABB / RAPS coverage)

change: On September 25-26, 2024 Pfizer voluntarily withdrew voxelotor (Oxbryta) for sickle cell disease from all markets after postmarketing data showed more vaso-occlusive crises and deaths versus placebo. The FDA advised clinicians to stop prescribing it.
practice_impact: Voxelotor is no longer an available SCD answer. Remaining options are hydroxyurea (first line), L-glutamine, crizanlizumab, transfusion, and gene therapies (exa-cel, lovo-cel).
source: FDA / Pfizer voluntary withdrawal of Oxbryta (voxelotor), 2024 (Epocrates coverage)

change: On May 16, 2025 the FDA issued a Drug Safety Communication warning of rare but severe pruritus after stopping long-term daily cetirizine or levocetirizine. Onset is typically within 1-5 days in patients who used the drug for months to years. The FDA added the warning to prescription labeling and plans OTC Drug Facts updates.
practice_impact: Counsel patients on chronic daily cetirizine or levocetirizine about rebound pruritus on discontinuation. Symptoms may resolve on restarting; consider a gradual taper.
source: FDA Drug Safety Communication, FDA requires warning about rare but severe itching after stopping long-term use of cetirizine or levocetirizine, 2025
